summary: Iteration 13 verifies the bug fix for 'Logos are not being added to social queue images' on PATCH /api/social/posts/{id}/logo-position. Previously the endpoint silently swallowed every failure mode (missing raw_filename, missing logo file, missing primary_logo on org, compose helper missing) and returned 200, causing the frontend to show 'Logo applied' success while nothing actually changed. The endpoint now returns descriptive 422 errors for every failure path AND falls back to image.filename as the base for legacy posts (with_logo=False, no raw_filename). Created /app/backend/tests/test_social_logo_position.py with 13 tests covering all 7 review-mandated scenarios + 5-anchor regression. ALL 13 PASS in 1.77s. Frontend not retested per review note ('the frontend change is zero-lines; only the backend behaviour changed'). Existing test_social_image_logo.py regression suite (generate-image still composites logo on fresh images) — all 7 tests pass (~104s).
critical_code_review_comments: social_posts.py:668-689 the legacy fallback `if not base_filename and not existing_img.get('with_logo'): base_filename = existing_img.get('filename')` is correct — it ONLY fires when with_logo is False, so it cannot double-brand an already-composited image. The double-brand guard at line 683 (raise 422 when base_filename is empty AND with_logo=True with no raw) is logically reached by the same code path. Verified empirically by TestErrorPaths::test_double_brand_guard.
social_posts.py:647 position whitelist check happens BEFORE find_one — correct (returns 422 fast for invalid position even if post id is missing). Tested.

social_posts.py:691 `if compose_logo_on_image is None or not upload_dir: raise HTTPException(500, ...)` — defensive, returns 500 not 422 because this is a server config bug, not a user-fixable input issue. Good distinction.

social_posts.py:714-719 update payload sets raw_filename to base_filename, which (for legacy posts) is the original image.filename — this means a SECOND PATCH on the same legacy post will use the saved raw_filename and stay on the un-composited base, never compounding. Verified: TestLegacyFallback creates a legacy post, PATCHes once, the response has raw_filename=base_fn (original filename) — subsequent PATCHes would treat it as a modern post.

Error messages are EXACT string matches as required by the FE toast surfacing — assertions in TestErrorPaths verify each message verbatim (the double-brand assertion uses startswith because the human string includes a trailing 'Click Regenerate...' clause beyond the short version in the brief; both are present in the source).

MINOR: The double-brand 422 message in source includes an additional trailing sentence ("Click 'Regenerate' to produce a fresh image with the logo.") that isn't in the review-request error-message spec but is helpful UX. The test asserts startswith() to remain robust to either form.

context_for_next_testing_agent: test_social_logo_position.py is the canonical regression harness for PATCH /social/posts/{id}/logo-position. Key trick: each test runs in its own asyncio event loop with a fresh AsyncIOMotorClient(io_loop=loop) — motor binds the client to the loop where IO first happens, so re-using a module-scoped client across pytest test functions causes 'Event loop is closed' errors. The `_run(coro_factory)` helper handles this. To extend: drop new error-path tests as additional methods in TestErrorPaths and use _put_disk_image() + _insert_post(org_id, image) helpers — the fixture `ctx` already gives you a logged-in session and an org with a real primary logo on disk. Real LLM is NOT called in this file; only the existing test_social_image_logo.py hits Nano Banana (~100s, runs slow when in suite).
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: Pre-fix, reposition_logo() wrapped the entire compose pipeline in a permissive try/except path: it (a) didn't validate that the post actually had an image, (b) didn't validate that the org had a primary_logo on file, (c) didn't validate the logo file existed on disk, (d) didn't validate the base file existed on disk, and (e) didn't fall back when raw_filename was missing on legacy posts. When ANY of these silently failed, the endpoint still returned 200 with the unchanged image dict, so the frontend's `toast.success('Logo applied')` fired without any state change. The user clicked 'Apply primary logo' on their deployed instance, saw success, but the with_logo flag never flipped on the card. FIX: every failure mode now raises HTTPException(422, '<exact human message>') and the frontend's existing `err.response.data.detail` toast surfaces them verbatim. Additionally, a legacy-post recovery path was added: when image has no raw_filename AND with_logo=False, treat image.filename as the un-composited source — this rescues the user's old posts that were generated before raw_filename was persisted (the case for the user's deployed-instance posts on pro.soulprintengine.ai). REPRO: insert {image:{filename:'x.png',with_logo:False}} into social_posts (no raw_filename), PATCH /logo-position?position=top-left. Pre-fix: 200 with image unchanged. Post-fix: 200 with new composed-* file and with_logo=True (legacy fallback) — verified in TestLegacyFallback::test_legacy_post_uses_filename_as_base. MITIGATION: deploy the fix; existing legacy posts will heal on first user click; new posts always carry raw_filename so subsequent reposition is cheap and never falls into the legacy branch.
